#3397. I tested the Google Pixel Tag and it’s the most findable tracker for Android phones — plus it does something Apple AirTag can't

Keep exploring and earning more as a member.

Unlock and manage exclusive Tom’s Guide member rewards.

Join the Tom's Guide Club for quick access. Enter your email below and we'll send confirmation, and sign you up to our newsletter.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The Pixel Tag delivers an outstanding tracking experience for Android users, matching the AirTag’s $29 price point while beating it out with superior Precision Finding range and persistent alerts when the batter level gets low.

Why you can trust Tom's Guide Our writers and editors spend hours analyzing and reviewing products, services, and apps to help find what's best for you. Find out more about how we test, analyze, and rate.

Over the past few years, I’ve tested my fair share of Bluetooth trackers — ranging from wallet-thin cards like the Statik SmartCard Incognito to the Pebblebee Halo, which can potentially help elderly individuals in emergency situations. Google has expanded its Find Hub network, finally giving Android users plenty of options, but many of these trackers share one glaring limitation: pinpoint proximity tracking.

While iPhone users have long enjoyed the superb performance of Precision Finding — leaning on Ultra Wideband (UWB) for pinpoint accuracy — most Android trackers don’t have that luxury. Instead, they rely on basic Bluetooth proximity that only shows broad geographic circles on a map.

Google’s Pixel Tag is one of the few Android trackers that packages Ultra Wideband (UWB) and Bluetooth Channel Sounding directly into Google’s native ecosystem. As a result, the Pixel Tag delivers true visual Precision Finding to Android devices. After putting it to the test, I found it holds one distinct advantage over the AirTag and one of the best Bluetooth trackers you can get.

Ultra-Wideband (UWB) + Bluetooth Channel Sounding

Easily the best feature of the Pixel Tag is its ability to lock down an exact position with outstanding Precision Finding range, which actually managed to outperform even Apple's AirTag 2 in my testing. Using the Find My Device app on an Android phone, you get intuitive on-screen visual guidance, complete with compass-like directional arrows and real-time distance readouts that point you right where you need to go.

While the AirTag 2 tapped out around 74 feet in my testing before dropping its Ultra Wideband connection, the Pixel Tag held on slightly farther, reaching roughly 82 feet. That extra reach eliminates the guesswork of tracking down misplaced gear, like my keys when I've completely forgotten where I left them. Plus, you can still trigger a loud audio chime if the tag slips deep between couch cushions and you can't spot it right away.

The AirTag has an unmistakable look, but Google has delivered an equally compelling design — especially when it comes to size. At just 5.4mm thick, the Pixel Tag is significantly sleeker than the AirTag, making it far less conspicuous when slipped into a standard wallet. With its minimalist, matte-finished polycarbonate body, I really dig the pebble-like aesthetic, which does a far better job of masking smudges and fingerprints than the AirTag's scratch-prone stainless steel back.

Even with that slimmed-down profile, Google didn’t cut corners on durability, outfitting it with a rugged IP67 dust- and water-resistance rating. Plus, swapping out the CR2032 coin-cell battery is painless — all it takes is a quick twist of the back cover.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Beyond tracking down my keys, wallet, backpack, or other gear, the Pixel Tag offers another standout feature you won’t find on the AirTag: the ability to ring your phone. With a simple double-press of the physical button on the front, you can instantly trigger your phone to ring at full volume — even if it's set to silent or vibrate. This reverse-finding capability is a lifesaver in a crunch when you're rushing out the door and can't find your phone anywhere.

One of the biggest annoyances I have with the AirTag is discovering weeks or even months later that it's dead. Sure, my iPhone might have sent a low-battery notification, but those alerts are easy to forget. That’s why I’m stoked about the Pixel Tag’s persistent automated reminders, which offer huge peace of mind if I overlook that initial heads-up.

Google rates the user-replaceable CR2032 coin-cell battery for up to a full year of typical use. While I haven’t had the Pixel Tag long enough to drain it down and trigger an alert firsthand, knowing Find Hub will send a notification “every 2 weeks until it’s replaced” ensures it won't quietly drop off my radar. Usually, I’m not a fan of that level of notification nagging, but in this case, it's a welcome safety net.

Despite having some key advantages over the AirTag, there’s one area where the Pixel Tag falls behind its rival: accessory availability. You can find an AirTag mount, leather loop, rugged clip, or pet collar attachment with a quick search online. The Pixel Tag, however, launches with very few options.

In fact, Google doesn't even offer any official accessories right out of the gate. The only ones I’ve been able to track down so far are basic silicone cases from Walmart. Because the Pixel Tag’s design doesn't include a built-in lanyard hole or keyring cutout, you'll need a dedicated case or adhesive mount just to attach it to your keys or backpack. For early adopters, finding the exact style or mount you want right now will require some patience while third-party makers ramp up production.

Considering how long the Pixel line has been around, you’d think Google would’ve come out with its own AirTag rival sooner. Even so, the Pixel Tag is a long-overdue addition — and it’s easily one of the most capable and well-rounded Bluetooth trackers on the market.

Between its class-leading Precision Finding range, compact design, and reverse-phone-ringing feature, it addresses the pinpoint tracking compromises that have long plagued the Android ecosystem. The only other real alternatives with Ultra Wideband support are Motorola’s Moto Tag and Samsung’s SmartTag3. You still get all the essential safeguards expected from a flagship tracker, too, including left-behind alerts and a dedicated Lost Mode that allows anyone who finds your gear to scan it and get in touch.

At $29 for a single one (or $99 for a four-pack), Google matches Apple dollar for dollar — but delivers greater range and features the AirTag simply can’t match.

Previously, he held editor roles with PhoneArena, Android Authority, Digital Trends, and SPY. #3395. Samsung’s Newest Flagship Soundbar System Is $500 Off Ahead of Black Friday

Pradershika Sharma is a tech deals writer for Lifehacker. She has a Master’s degree in English Literature, a B.Ed., and a TESOL certification. She has been writing professionally since 2018, creating product reviews, affiliate articles, and search ads for global clients while working with Rubix Agency and Cognizant. Previously, she spent a year teaching English at the junior high level.An avid reader since childhood, Pradershika's idea of extreme sports is staying up to read “just one more chapter.” She lives in India.

Samsung’s flagship soundbars have reached the point where the yearly upgrades are more about refinement than reinvention, and that is pretty much the story with the Samsung HW-Q990H—and with Black Friday approaching, this 2026 model is already seeing a $500 discount, bringing its price down to $1,497.99 from $1,997.99. That's its lowest price to date, according to price trackers.

Samsung kept the same 11.1.4-channel setup from the older HW-Q990F, including the soundbar, wireless subwoofer, and two rear speakers, but leaned harder into software this time around—features like the SpaceFit Sound Pro automatically adjust the sound depending on your room layout, and unlike some auto-calibration features that barely change anything, this one reportedly shifts the audio balance in noticeable ways. Sometimes it improves dialogue clarity and bass response. Other times, you may prefer tweaking things yourself with the built-in seven-band EQ.

The system also handles basically every major audio format, supports wireless Dolby Atmos with compatible Samsung TVs, and includes 4K 120Hz HDMI passthrough for people gaming on a PlayStation 5 or Xbox Series X. That said, while the bass is strong for a compact subwoofer, it compresses when you push the volume near maximum, so it's not perfect for huge spaces or people who want nightclub-level output. More importantly, if you already own the HW-Q990F or even the older HW-Q990D, upgrading probably will not feel dramatic enough to justify the cost. But for someone starting from TV speakers or an entry-level soundbar, this system can completely change how movies, games, and even sports feel at home.

Black Friday sales officially begin Friday, Nov. 27, 2026, and run throughout “Cyber Week,” the five-day period that runs from Thanksgiving through Cyber Monday,  Nov. 30, 2026. But Black Friday and Cyber Monday dates have expanded as retailers compete for customers. You can get the same Black Friday sales early, and we expect sales to wind down by Dec. 2, 2026.

Nowadays, both large retailers and small businesses compete for Black Friday shoppers, so you can expect practically every store to run sales through Monday, Nov. 30, 2026. The “best” sales depend on your needs, but in general, the biggest discounts tend to come from larger retailers who can afford lower prices: think places like Amazon, Walmart, Target, Best Buy, and Home Depot. You can find all the best sales from major retailers on our Black Friday coverage.

Yes, Amazon has Black Friday sales, but prices aren’t always what they seem. Use a price tracker to make sure you’re getting the best deal, or refer to guides like our live blog that use price trackers for you. And if you have an Amazon Prime membership, make the most of it.

#3392. The Perfect 'Friends' Cast if the Sitcom Were Made Today

Fancasting is a popular pastime. Don't you love to look at classic shows, wonder what the characters might look like if the show were made today, then picture current celebrities in the key and supporting roles? Friends is the perfect show to do this with. The iconic sitcom features a mixed bag of personalities. It's famously known for lacking diversity, and you can't help but wonder who might play each of the characters in a modern-day version.

The way the characters look might change, but with the right actors playing them, their essence would remain. Consider that while most of the cast was in their mid-to-late 20s and early 30s when the series started, celebrities today tend to look younger than ever. That means casting a 35-to-40-year-old wouldn't be out of the realm of possibility. When you consider who's hot right now, a few names stand out as actors who could nail these characters in a modern-day dream casting scenario.

Sydney Sweeney is this generation's "it" girl — a status that Jennifer Aniston, who played Rachel Green, understood all too well at the height of Friends' success. Sweeney has proven herself capable of handling both drama and comedy in shows like Euphoria. Though that HBO series has some of the heaviest TV episodes of the last 20 years, there are also lighter moments. Sweeney's whiny and at times insufferable character Cassie sometimes delivers laughs, whether intentionally or unintentionally. Sweeney also starred in the romantic comedy Anyone But You, where she showed off more of her comedy talents.

She has the same distinct look Aniston does — a beauty that stands out from others. We could totally see whoever plays Ross having pined for her since they were in high school. And Sweeney would be believable as the runaway bride who works as a waitress in a coffee shop until pursuing a career in fashion.

Honorable mentions: Jenna Ortega (her comedic timing is brilliant); Zendaya (she's a consummate pro who can tackle any role).

Fans either loved or hated Ross, played by David Schwimmer, who came across as annoying and complaining at times. But deep down, he was a good guy who not everyone understood. He lacked confidence in himself and couldn't seem to figure out his love life until the bitter end of the show.

Jesse Eisenberg is a perfect actor to play him. He's known for playing anxious characters, which fits right into the Ross wheelhouse. His characters are often intelligent, but also socially awkward like Ross. From portraying Mark Zuckerberg in The Social Network to the illusionist in Now You See Me, one of those perfect action movies anyone can enjoy, his resume speaks for itself. While he's already in his 40s, Eisenberg still has a boyish face, so he could pull off early 30s.

Honorable mentions: Jay Baruchel (he plays the awkwardly confident nerd so well); Tyler James Williams (his uptight and awkward character in Abbott Elementary proves he has what it takes).

It would take a huge actor to tackle the role of Chandler Bing, and Daniel Radcliffe could be a good fit. While he's best known for playing Harry Potter in that massive franchise, it's easy to forget that he also portrayed "Weird Al" Yankovic in the musical parody Weird: The Al Yankovic Story. He's also currently killing it in the sitcom The Rise and Fall of Reggie Dinkins. He knows how to command a screen like the late Matthew Perry does, and he has demonstrated his skill for comedic timing as well.

Chandler often used sarcasm and self-deprecation to hide his insecurities, and we could totally see Radcliffe doing the same. He isn't afraid to be silly either, playing everything from a flatulent dead body in Swiss Army Man to several humorous characters in Miracle Workers. Though older than Perry was when he started on Friends, Radcliffe forever has that youthful look.

Honorable mentions: Skylar Astin (he has a similar look and a reputation for playing sweet and likable characters); Joe Keery (the flowing hair and talent for sarcasm in Stranger Things make him a viable candidate).

Four of the largest communities on the planet, and four completely different reasons to belong to one. Here is yours, what it would give you, and the argument you would be having within a week.

You belong to the fandom that is really about comfort. Hogwarts works on people because it is a place rather than a plot, and the pull is not the wizard war so much as the corridors, the food, the weather and the sense that somebody is expecting you.

You belong to the deepest fandom on this list, the one where somebody has always read further than you and is quietly delighted to say so. Middle-earth rewards patience more than any other world in popular culture.

You belong to the loudest and largest tent of the four, the one where three generations are all watching the same thing and none of them agree about any of it. That disagreement is not a flaw in this fandom, it is the main activity.

You belong to the thinking fandom, the one that turns up for the argument rather than the explosion. Trek has always been a series of ethical problems in space, and the people who love it love being asked what they would have done.

Anya Taylor-Joy is one of the most sought-after young actors of this generation. Rising to fame in The Queen's Gambit, one of the greatest miniseries masterpieces of the 21st century, then the movie The Menu, and now most recently starring in the Apple TV series Lucky, she has taken on diverse characters. While many have a certain sex appeal, Monica, originally played by Courteney Cox, is more upright. But Taylor-Joy is the type of actor you know could handle any type of character that's thrown at her.

This version of Monica might have to change slightly, but we could see it working. She could be a cute pairing with Radcliffe, Astin, or Keery, and I could see Eisenberg as her annoying older brother. It would be a role out of Taylor-Joy's usual darker, more intense shows and movies, but she could be convincing as the uptight, neat-freak, hard-working chef.

Honorable mentions: Hailee Steinfeld (she has the same adorably magnetic quality); Millie Bobby Brown (she has a sweet innocence about her like Monica); Ayo Edebiri (she'd taps into Monica's sarcastic side); Chase Infiniti (she has the same classic beauty and tremendous acting talent); Maude Apatow (she's an up-and-comer whose Euphoria character you could imagine as being a younger Monica).

Matt LeBlanc beautifully portrayed the handsome but goofy and not very academically intelligent friend. This is a character type Dave Franco knows all too well and could play to a T. He leaned into the comedy angle in movies like Superbad and the Now You See Me films, as well as in shows like The Afterparty and The Studio, the latter of which he played an embellished version of himself.

While Franco is already 40, his boyish face would fit with a more mature version of the character. He could easily replicate Joey's doe-eyed look, womanizing ways, and adorably naïve personality.

Honorable mentions: Zac Efron (he fits the hunky persona and knows comedy); Timothée Chalamet (he's a versatile young actor who can take on any role); Robbie Amell (he's dabbled in comedy with Upload, showing he can handle goofy, macho roles).

It's tough to imagine anyone but Lisa Kudrow embodying Phoebe. But when considering the younger generation of actors, Haley Lu Richardson is easy to picture in a boho outfit, playing her guitar in the coffee shop, singing about her smelly cat, and playing up the eccentric, kooky personality.

Richardson has shown her range in roles like The White Lotus, one of the most perfect HBO shows of the last 15 years, where she played a young assistant trying to find herself. She more recently appeared in the Peacock series Ponies as a confident and rebellious wife of a CIA agent in the '70s. There's no doubt she'd tackle Phoebe with a modern 21st-century twist.

Honorable mentions: Elle Fanning (she's one of the most versatile young actors of this generation); Sadie Sink (the sarcastic slant of Max in Stranger Things would be perfect for the character); Hunter Schafer (her nuanced performance in Euphoria included some comedy as well); Emma Myers (her upbeat character in Wednesday has hints of Phoebe).

The late James Michael Tyler quietly played Gunther, the manager of Central Perk who not-so-secretly pined for Rachel. He quietly puts up with the antics of the group and keeps their favorite couch perpetually reserved so it's always available to them when they want it. For a time, he was Rachel's boss when she worked there as a waitress.

Suraj Sharma feels like a good actor for this role, perhaps because of his role as Sid in the short-lived How I Met Your Mother spin-off, How I Met Your Father. On that show, he's a member of the core group who happens to own a bar. Even though he's part of the friend group, they often visit the bar while he's working. Beyond that, he could lend more personality to the role, since Tyler was mostly a background character with a few lines here and there. Sharma has great comedic timing, so even with a single line, he'd command attention and garner laughs.

Honorable mention: Reba McEntire (she would bring loads more comedy to the role with some good one-liners).

For some time, Monica dated the handsome Richard, played by the handsome Tom Selleck. He was tall, suave, wealthy, and much older. Unsurprisingly, Chandler was threatened by Richard when he felt like the old beau might return to Monica's life. In this generation, I could easily see Jacob Elordi playing Richard. He's tall and handsome as well, and while young, there's no reason Richard couldn't be switched to a young, successful businessman instead of an older one.

Given the shift to female empowerment nowadays, it wouldn't be out of the ordinary to have Monica dating a younger man and swapping the story angle. Elordi, for his part, knows how to play the prince charming type, having done so in projects like The Kissing Booth and Wuthering Heights.

Honorable mentions: Liam Hemsworth (has the same classic handsome look); Robert Pattinson (his characters often have an air of mystery about them); Glen Powell (his smile lights a room, and he'd easily fit as the ex that makes Chandler jealous).

Aside from Monica, Chandler had one other major girlfriend through the show's run. Janice (Maggie Wheeler) is best known for her distinct accent, loud personality, bold clothing choices, and obnoxious cries of, "Oh my god!" Isabela Merced is an up-and-coming young actor who is best known for her role in The Last of Us. But her experience from Nickelodeon shows, as well as more serious ones like in Alien: Romulus, suggest this could be a fun role to show her comedic side, too.

Janice appears in multiple seasons of Friends, coming back into Chandler's life more than once. Sometimes, the group just runs into her in various scenarios. Merced proved in Season 2 of The Last of Us that she could dominate scenes. That's something Wheeler did whenever the camera was on her as Janice, oozing main character energy even though she wasn't one.

Honorable mentions: Joey King (her range is tremendous, and though she mostly does serious roles, she'd ace this one); Melissa Rauch (she perfected the nasally, squeaky voice for Bernadette on The Big Bang Theory).

I mean, could anyone else possibly play Mike, Phoebe's long-term boyfriend and eventual husband, other than Paul Rudd himself? Sure, decades have passed since he last played the role, but as many joke, Rudd doesn't seem to age. He still looks like he did back then, so it would be hilarious to have Rudd return in this same role.

The age difference might be a little unsettling, depending on who's playing Phoebe, but would it really be any different than when Selleck played the older Richard dating Monica? Rudd has such a boyish charm that he'd slink so easily back into the role that everyone would forget he's pushing 60 and totally believe that Phoebe has fallen head over heels for the weirdly wonderful pianist and former lawyer.

#3391. I Played Wendy's RPG, and It's Actually Worth It for the Free Food

November is a huge month for video games. Nintendo dropped its remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for the Switch 2 last week, and the long-awaited Grand Theft Auto VI is right around the corner. But the game we've been waiting for most of all also launched this month: WendyQuest, the free RPG from Wendy's. (No, this is not a joke.)

Despite the absurdity of a hamburger chain making a full video game (complete with Wendy's-themed puns), the thing is, this game is pretty solid—even if it is a promotion at the end of the day. WendyQuest's main purpose is to offer customers coupons they can use toward purchases in real life, though it's a bit of a commitment. It took me just under an hour of gameplay before I earned my first coupon, and Wendy's says it takes roughly 15 hours to beat. All that to say, this is a pretty unique marketing campaign.

I was surprised booting up WendyQuest on my iPhone. This doesn't necessarily feel like a thrown-together product. On the flip side, the production quality is quite high. The music is solid and very much traditionally RPG; there are even three save slots, in case you plan to return to this RPG again and again.

There's even a story, albeit cheesy (no pun intended): As the game explains, the "Four Great Spirits of Flavor" created Savoria, "a food-rich paradise." All was well until Mech Corp, led by the evil Dr. MechBorg, built robots to take over Savoria. The plot is far from compelling, and the writing can be a little over the top, but hey, I'll give them credit: They thought through a full story here.

You play as Wendy, the "representation of true culinary excellence and taste as dictated by the four ancient spirits of flavor." Wendy (or The Wendy, as some call her) is tasked with saving the world, traveling between villages and picking up new characters along the way. The game world even has "real" Wendy's locations you can visit. These act like inns and shops in other RPGs, giving you a chance to heal while also buying equipment.

Like other RPGs, WendyQuest uses turn-based combat. You have to charge up your attacks, but stop before they hit 100%, or you'll miss. (It took me a while to master the timing.) I'm pretty impressed with how challenging some of these battles can be, though you are quickly given the option of an amulet that gives you a huge leg-up in combat. You don't have to take it, but it makes fights easier if you're only in it for the coupons. That, combined with the spatulas the game encourages you to buy, lets you mow down enemies. You can also utilize your companions here: "Frygor," for example, can either attack enemies with a barrage of fries, or use those fries to build a shield to protect you.

While there are tons of enemies to fight, the key baddies are the "mechs." There are five in total, and after you defeat each, you get a coupon. Spoiler alert: The first mech drops the "Fry Stone," which nets you a coupon for a free order of medium fries—though you need to buy something in tandem, as well as use the Wendy's app. While I stopped my gaming here for this article, the other four coupons are:

Free biscuit or croissant (I didn't even know Wendy's sold biscuits and croissants)

Again, it's wild that WendyQuest has a 10+ hour campaign, with over 1,000 lines of dialogue to boot. I'm not sure this is a game I'm going to see through to the end, but I'll admit, it's a fun marketing approach from Wendy's. Sure, they could have run a promotion in the Wendy's app to give people coupons, but instead, they built an entire RPG. I respect it. You can download the game for iOS, Android, or Steam.

#3378. Update Your iPhone to Prevent People From Seeing iMessages They Shouldn't

Has this ever happened to you? You add someone new to an iMessage group chat, and wonder, "Huh, can they see any of the messages from before they were added?" The answer to that question is supposed to be "no." By design, new iMessage group chat members are only privy to texts that arrive after they were added. When they join, it's essentially a blank slate, as if you just created the group for the first time. At least, that's how it's intended to work.

As it turns out, there's a bug with iMessage that may allow new group chat members to see texts from before they were added to the chat. That's a problem, and not just for the iPhone users out there talking smack about people before inviting them to join the group chat. It means iMessage, and Apple's platforms in general, aren't working like they're supposed to be. You don't have to be talking behind people's backs to not want new members seeing existing chats. Maybe you're planning a surprise party for someone, and add them to the group once everyone's in on the plan; maybe the texts in the chat aren't relevant to the current group, and the person joining simply does not need to access them.

That's not all: There exists another security flaw that could allow remote hackers to join an iMessage group and receive new messages. You might add a new user to a group chat and inadvertently invite them to read all existing messages, while at the same time being attacked by a bad actor who can then intercept all future messages. Not good.

Luckily, there's currently a fix for these problems. Apple patched (and revealed) the bugs, along with seven other security flaws, with a series of software updates on Monday for iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, and Vision Pro. Not all of the updates include patches for these two iMessage flaws—specifically, some of the updates for older Apple devices. But the rest, including iOS 27.2.1, macOS 27.2.1, macOS 26.7.3, macOS 15.8.3, watchOS 27.2.1, and visionOS 27.2.1, include the iMessage patches.

Each update includes its own list of patches, but, for this article, I'll take a look at the nine patches in iOS 27.2.1. You'll find the two iMessage bugs, plus seven other patches, in the list below:

AirPlay: Impact: An attacker in Bluetooth range may be able to bypass the rate limit on pairing code attempts. Description: A logic issue was addressed with improved state management. CVE-2026-113968: Apple

App Intents: Impact: An app may be able to access sensitive user data. Description: An authorization issue was addressed with improved state management. CVE-2026-113963: László Várady

Bluetooth: Impact: An attacker in Bluetooth range may be able to corrupt process memory. Description: A use-after-free issue was addressed with improved memory management. CVE-2026-113970: Apple

brotli: Impact: Processing maliciously crafted input may lead to memory corruption. Description: An out-of-bounds write issue was addressed with improved input validation. CVE-2026-111497

CoreUtils: Impact: A malicious Bluetooth device may be able to establish a pairing without user interaction. Description: This issue was addressed with improved checks. CVE-2026-113965: Apple

CoreUtils: Impact: An attacker in Bluetooth range may be able to bypass the rate limit on pairing code attempts and pair with a device without user interaction. Description: A logic issue was addressed with improved state management. CVE-2026-113964: an anonymous researcher

Messages: Impact: A remote attacker may be able to join an iMessage group chat and receive its messages. Description: An authorization issue was addressed with improved validation. CVE-2026-113961: an anonymous researcher

Messages: Impact: A user added to an iMessage group may be able to access messages sent before they joined. Description: This issue was addressed by removing the vulnerable code. CVE-2026-113960: an anonymous researcher

Rapportd: Impact: An attacker on the same network may be able to bypass the rate limit on AirPlay pairing code attempts. Description: A logic issue was addressed with improved state management. CVE-2026-113969: Apple

For a full accounting of the patches included in the other security updates, check out Apple's official security releases site.

To install Apple's latest security updates, you'll simply need to update your device as you usually do. On iPhone, iPad, Apple Watch, and Vision Pro, head to Settings > General > Software Update; on Mac, go to System Settings > General > Software Update. Here, follow the on-screen instructions to download and install the latest version of your device's software.

#3374. This AirPods Feature Fixed My Biggest Problem With Listening to Podcasts to Fall Asleep

We're highlighting the small changes—from useful new gadgets, to fresh productivity techniques, to efficient hacks—that are improving our lives on a weekly basis.

There's lots to recommend about podcasts (and lots of podcasts to recommend), but one of their biggest benefits—for me, anyway—has little to do with what a particular show is about or even who hosts it: They're great for dissociating. I often have a podcast playing to distract my anxious brain from whatever I'm worried about (which, in 2026, is usually slightly less than everything).

Any time I don't want to be alone with my thoughts (say, when commuting or doing mindless chores), I can put on a podcast and be entertained by a couple of goobers talking about movies rather than spinning my wheels about my son's middle school applications. And there's no time I want to disassociate from reality more than bedtime.

For years I've used podcasts as a non-pharmaceutical sleep aid, and few things are more effective at helping me drop off quickly. Unfortunately, for years this also meant that once I fell asleep, the podcast kept playing. I have my podcast app set to delete episodes once finished, so if it was a show I cared about, I'd need to do a lot of redownloading and scrubbing through to find where I left off—that is, until I upgraded my earbuds to the AirPods Pro 3.

The AirPods Pro 3 launched alongside iOS 26 in the fall of 2025 with flashy features like vastly improved noise cancellation, Live Translation, Heart Rate Sensing, and hearing health settings, all of them quite welcome on a set of $250 premium earbuds. But the best new AirPods feature was one I didn't even know about when I decided to upgrade my four-year-old Beats Fit Pro.

In the AirPods settings (accessible via your iPhone's Settings app), if you tap Audio & Routing and scroll down, you'll see an option to turn on a setting called Pause Media When Falling Asleep. I don't think I need to tell you what this setting does. I can tell you that it works great.

According to Apple, the feature works by sensing when you're drifting off using the earbuds' built-in accelerometer to track your movement (or lack thereof). Once your earbuds have determined that you're falling asleep, they will pause your audio for you. And it isn't just the 2025 AirPods Pro 3 that support it—it also works on the second-generation AirPods Pro as well as the AirPods 4 and the AirPods 5.

I'll admit that I don't really understand how the AirPods Pro 3 can tell I'm falling asleep versus just lying very still, but I've never had them pause accidentally during active listening. Conversely, whenever I go back to the podcast I was listening to the night before, I'll find that the audio paused within a minute or two of the last part I remember hearing.

The AirPods Pro 3 aren't the only earbuds with a feature like this, but you'll most often only find it in dedicated "sleep earbuds" designed specifically for the purpose. While many of those offer extra health features like the ability to track your sleep cycles, I'm not really interested in that (my Apple Watch does most of it, and I don't look at that data anyway). Pausing my audio when I'm asleep is really all I need, and the AirPods Pro 3 do it well enough that I don't need to bother with a pair of dedicated bedtime buds.

#3370. MagSafe Monday: Pelican’s MagSafe wallet is built for the people who still carry cash

I’ve been on a Pelican kick this fall. It started with the Pelican MagSafe Wallet, then the Pelican MagSafe Battery Pack, and the reason is pretty simple: once the weather turns cool, I want iPhone accessories built for the outdoors because I am outside more. The Pelican Protector Magnetic Money Clip Wallet is really helpful is you want something rugged, but also supports holding cash.

MagSafe Monday: Every Monday, Bradley Chambers looks at the latest and greatest in the MagSafe and wireless charging industry to help you get the most out of your Apple devices that support wireless charging.

Most magnetic wallets are a simple card sleeve and nothing else. If you carry a few $5 bills for tips, cash-only places, etc., you end up folding them around a card and hoping they don’t slip out. The Pelican Protector Magnetic Money Clip Wallet has a stainless steel money clip on the outside of the wallet, so the cash rides on the back, where you can access it without pulling your credit cards out. It’s the same hard-shell construction as the rest of Pelican’s lineup, with the same MagSafe magnets.

The wallet holds up to five cards, which is just about perfect for my use cases. That covers my Driver’s license, debit card, and a few credit cards. There are ridges inside that push the cards up when you squeeze, so you’re not digging with your nails. A steel plate blocks RFID scanning, and the shell is rated IPX4 for water, which covers rain, etc.

Pelican calls its drop protection military-grade, which is what every accessory company says. A more useful way to think about it is that it’s a hard-shell wallet rather than a leather or silicone one.

Two things to know going in with this wallet. Five cards plus a clip of cash makes for a thick back on your phone, so this isn’t a very slim wallet. If you’re replacing a money clip, you are basically combining the two into one.

If you never carry much cash, the original Pelican wallet is the better pick. If you do want to carry a bunch of cash, the Pelican Protector Magnetic Money Clip Wallet is an awesome pickup.

#3369. Yella Beezy Convicted of Hiring Hitman to Kill Rapper Mo3, Sentenced to Life

Yella Beezy is going to prison for the rest of his life ... the Dallas rapper has been convicted of hiring a hitman to murder fellow rapper Mo3 in a brazen shooting on a busy Texas highway.

A Dallas jury found Beezy -- whose legal name is Markies Conway -- guilty of capital murder Wednesday ... exactly six years after Mo3 was gunned down on Interstate 35 in November 2020.

He was sentenced to life in prison without the possibility of parole.

Prosecutors said Beezy paid Kewon White $40,000 to carry out the killing following a years-long feud between the rappers. White chased Mo3 -- real name Melvin Noble -- onto the highway and opened fire, killing the 28-year-old and wounding a bystander.

Beezy's defense maintained his innocence, arguing prosecutors built their case on speculation rather than solid evidence ... but jurors weren't buying it. White was also convicted of capital murder in September and sentenced to life without parole.

As TMZ previously reported ... Beezy was arrested in March 2025 in connection with Mo3's murder, and prosecutors later released video showing the deadly highway shooting. Mo3 got out of his vehicle and tried to run from the gunman on the busy interstate ... but was shot and killed as he fled.

Beezy was released from jail after posting bond later that month ... though a judge subsequently denied his request to modify his bond conditions.

He is now headed behind bars for life ... joining White, who's already serving the same sentence.

Google just announced its November Pixel Drop, which adds a slew of new features for Pixel phones and watches. Plus, the Pixel Tag officially goes on sale today (look out for our review here).

There's a ton of stuff in the drop, but some highlights include expanded Gemini Intelligence, a new Create My Widget feature and step-by-step workouts on Pixel Watch 3 and newer.

The company also announced its new Google Fi "Super Network." We've got more details about how it works here.

Let's dive into what's available and which devices support these new features.

For the most part, the big features are only coming to the Pixel 10 and Pixel 11 series phones in this update. Some smaller tools are available on Pixel 6 and later phones. Surprise, most of it is AI-related.

Starting with AI, Gemini Intelligence is now available on Pixel 10 phones, including the new Rambler feature, which automatically removes filler words and can format your spoken words into "clean, coherent" text. It also adds automations for specified apps, including grocery ordering, ridesharing and booking reservations.

Create My Widgets enables you to build custom widgets using AI by describing the type of tool you need. Google is also offering curated recommendations.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Gemini Call Screen is on Pixel 11 phones and screens calls on demand. For Pixel 10 and 11 phones, Gemini can make calls for you, doing things like checking inventory, putting items on hold, or making/changing reservations.

Pixel 11 phones are getting Pixel Solver, which uses generative AI to create custom templates and "conversational, multi-step problem solving for everyday" math.

Pixel 9 and above phones are getting Notification Summaries that will recap long conversations, giving you context at a glance.

The highlight feature, pun intended, is HiLight, announced at the Made By Google event in August. When your phone is face down, HiLight will glow to let you know if a favorite contact has sent you a message.

Otherwise, for 6a and above, there's a new Custom Icons style, which uses Nano Banana to generate. Transit Mode 2.0 triggers automatically based on phone sensors.

Pixel Search Updates lets you find content across your apps, web and settings using natural language search directly from the All Apps screen.

Unit Conversion is a module to help you skip toggling between the browser and the calculator. Pixel 6 and above phones are also getting Live Location Sharing for Pixel VIPs.

Finally, Pixel 10 phones are getting Extreme Charging Mode that quickly charges your phones to full.

Your Pixel Watch isn't getting as many features as the phones, but the big one is "Step-by-Step Workouts." Basically, your watch will give you step-by-step instructions for each exercise in your routine. It will also log reps, weights and track metrics from your Watch, or your phone.

This is available on Pixel Watch 3 and newer models.

Google announced that Create My Widgets, Gemini call Screen and Notification Summaries, outlined above, are "coming soon"; no specific date was provided.

Phone to Watch Unlock is also coming soon to Pixel Watch 3 and new models. This feature will let you unlock your watch with a nearby paired phone. No date was provided here either.

#3363. 10 Hacks Every Waze User Should Know

In addition to Lifehacker, her work has been featured on Wirecutter, Tom’s Guide, and ZDNET. Emily has also worked as a travel guide around the U.S. and as a content editor. She has a masters in social work and is a licensed therapist in Utah.

Waze is a crowdsourced navigation app designed to help you get where you're going as quickly and with as much information about your route as possible. Where Google Maps and Apple Maps offer relatively straightforward directions, Waze tries to outsmart these alternatives by integrating real-time community feedback about hazards, speed traps, road closures, and more. If you are switching to Waze or using it alongside your other navigation tools, these are the hacks to help you maximize everything the app has to offer.

If you find yourself losing track of time or running late for events, Waze can notify you when it's time to leave—based on your current location and live traffic—so you arrive on schedule. You can set up "Time to leave" reminders in advance for individual planned drives, or you can sync your calendar to receive notifications for scheduled events. Calendar sync connects to your device's default calendar app, but you can change this to a third-party alternative if you prefer. Calendar events must include a navigable address to trigger reminders, and you must select Plan a drive in Waze for the event.

Waze has a feature called "child reminders," which are notifications to check for children before you get out of the car. This is clearly an incredibly important use case, but you can also use these alerts for custom messages, like "Don't forget the groceries!" In Waze, tap the menu button > Settings > Reminders > Child reminder and select Custom message.

Variable speed limits, especially on unfamiliar routes, can result in you speeding when you don't mean to. But Waze can alert you if you exceed a customized speed threshold so you aren't caught by surprise or at higher risk of being ticketed. From the menu, go to Settings > Speedometer and turn on Show speedometer. Tap Speeding threshold to select what limit you want to trigger alerts, and turn on Alert at threshold if you want Waze to play a sound.

Waze offers a wealth of information on routes to help drivers navigate obstacles and hazards, but this can clutter your map and distract you from the most critical information, especially in congested, high-traffic areas. Waze says it limits and prioritizes alerts automatically, but you can actually customize which alerts you see based on what's most important to you. From the menu, go to Settings > Alerts and reports > Reports and select the relevant alerts.

In the same Alerts and reports menu, you can enable Alert while driving, which will give you an audio warning and an onscreen pop-up about your selected hazards. This allows you to run navigation via a different map app (like Google Maps or Apple Maps) in the foreground while still getting Waze data in the background.

Waze integrates with toll road and HOV lane passes, so if you have an express or fast lane subscription, your route will optimize for it. If you don't, Waze can still account for HOV lane eligibility if you tell it how many passengers are in your car. From the menu, go to Settings > Toll and HOV passes and tap the plus icon to add your pass(es) from the list. If you need to add your passenger count instead, you can do so from View routes and enable the HOV option.

If you're driving through an unfamiliar, highly congested, or poorly designed area, you can ask Waze to help you avoid tricky maneuvers, such as crossing multiple lanes of traffic or turning left at intersections without lights. This prioritizes ease over speed using protected green arrows, roundabouts, and right turns. From the menu, go to Settings > Navigation, Avoid difficult intersections and select Always. You can also ask Waze to avoid toll roads, ferries, freeways, and unpaved roads.

Waze has a built-in audio player that syncs with your preferred listening platform—such as Spotify, YouTube Music, and Pandora—so you can control your music without having to navigate between apps. (As Waze is a Google product, Apple Music isn't included.) Simply tap the music icon on the map to select your audio player and hit Accept. If you don't see the icon, go to Settings > Audio player and turn on Show on the map.

If you want to make audio directions more interesting, you can select a celebrity or character voice to help you navigate. Recent appearances include Bill Hader's Cat in the Hat and Ziggy Marley. Tap the speaker icon > Current voice to search for the voice or language you want to use. You can also record directions in your own voice.

#3361. Apple to open new Developer Center in Istanbul as part of broader Turkey investment

Apple today announced a long-term investment in Turkey, with seven new facilities focused on app development and manufacturing set to open in the country starting next year. Here are the details.

In a press release issued on its Turkish Newsroom (via MacRumors), Apple today announced a series of long-term investments in Turkey.

The announcement comes as former CEO and current executive chairman Tim Cook visits the country, as he’s been sharing on X.

Merhaba Istanbul! What a stunning view from the Grand Bazaar this morning alongside talented creator Cem Başak. Thrilled to visit this remarkable country! pic.twitter.com/c4daBBXe1l

The company’s investment in Turkey will be three-pronged, with the opening of five new Apple Developer Academies, one Apple Developer Center, and one Apple Manufacturing Academy.

Apple says it will open five new developer academies across Turkey over the next three years, with the first opening in Istanbul in 2027, alongside its new developer center. The Apple Manufacturing Academy, meanwhile, is set to open in Ankara in 2028.

Here’s Cook commenting on today’s announcement (translation ours):

“Apple has been serving our customers and communities in Turkey for 35 years. With this new commitment, we are proud to support the next generation of innovative entrepreneurs in the years ahead. […] Turkey’s developer community is developing apps used around the world. Meanwhile, small and medium-sized businesses stand out as organizations creating opportunities throughout the country. This investment provides developers and businesses with access to the training and resources they need to take their brightest ideas even further, as well as to Apple experts.”

Apple explained that its developer academies will offer “free, intensive nine-month programs focused on coding, design, marketing, project management, and artificial intelligence technologies,” while the developer center “will provide developers, entrepreneurs, and start-ups with a hands-on learning experience by providing access to the latest tools, technologies, and resources, as well as Apple experts and events.”

As for its manufacturing academy in Ankara, which will mark the company’s first Apple Manufacturing Academy outside the US, it will “provide free training and consultancy to small and medium-sized businesses, students and innovative entrepreneurs.”

Led by Apple experts, the curriculum will help participants adopt AI and intelligent manufacturing techniques through courses on machine learning technology, predictive maintenance, advanced automation, and robotics, as well as interactive workshops on lean operations and production efficiency.

Amazon is offering early Black Friday discounts on like-new versions of its 2024 Kindles, with prices starting at $152.99 for the Paperwhite and savings of $27 to $75 across five models that include the color-screen Colorsoft and the pen-equipped Kindle Scribe. All five are a generation behind Amazon's current lineup: The company introduced redesigned Paperwhite and Colorsoft models (plus accessories) in October, with the new Paperwhite now starting at $199.99, and replaced the 2024 Scribe with a third-generation model in December 2025. As for its “like-new” label, it means these are pre-owned devices that Amazon has tested and certified to look and work like new.

The Like-New Kindle Paperwhite (16GB) is down to $152.99 from $179.99 and covers just about everything most people need for everyday reading, including enough storage for thousands of ebooks. Its seven-inch, 300ppi glare-free display is larger than the previous generation’s 6.8-inch screen, with faster page turns, an adjustable warm light, IPX8 water resistance, and up to 12 weeks of battery life. As PCMag notes in its review, it's a great option for readers who don't need color or handwriting features.

The Like-New Kindle Paperwhite Signature Edition (32GB) is down to $190.99 from $224.99, making it just $38 more than the like-new Paperwhite (16GB). For that relatively small difference, you're doubling the storage to 32GB and getting wireless charging, an ad-free lock screen, and a front light that automatically adjusts to your surroundings—on top of the same sharp seven-inch display, IPX8 water resistance, and up to 12 weeks of battery life as the standard Paperwhite, as noted by this PCMag review.

The Like-New Kindle Colorsoft (16GB) is down to $220.99 from $260.99 and offers something the Paperwhite models can’t: a color E-Ink display, which makes it well suited to comics, graphic novels, illustrated books, and travel guides. Its seven-inch screen shows that color content at 150ppi while keeping text at a sharp 300ppi, and you can mark passages in multiple highlight colors to keep your notes organized. That said, colors are noticeably more muted than on a conventional tablet, and battery life tops out at eight weeks, compared with 12 weeks on the Paperwhite.

The Like-New Kindle Colorsoft Signature Edition (32GB) is down to $243.99 from $287.99, making it just $23 more than the standard like-new Colorsoft. For that modest increase, you're getting twice the storage at 32GB, which is particularly useful for comics, manga, and graphic novels that take up more space than regular ebooks, along with wireless charging, an automatically adjusting front light, and an ad-free lock screen. However, as PCMag notes in its review, the color display produces more subdued tones than a conventional tablet, so the Paperwhite remains the more economical choice if you primarily read novels.

The Like-New Kindle Scribe (16GB) is down to $284.99 from $359.99, the biggest dollar discount in this roundup. Unlike the other Kindles here, it's built for reading and writing, with a 10.2-inch, 300ppi glare-free display and a Premium Pen with an eraser and shortcut button—making it the most versatile option for readers who want an e-reader that doubles as a digital notebook.

In short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

Black Friday sales officially begin Friday, November 27, 2026, and run throughout “Cyber Week,” the five-day period that runs from Thanksgiving through Cyber Monday,  November 30, 2026. But Black Friday and Cyber Monday dates have expanded as retailers compete for customers. You can get the same Black Friday sales early, and we expect sales to wind down by December 2, 2026.

Yes, Amazon has Black Friday sales, but prices aren’t always what they seem. Use a price tracker to make sure you’re getting the best deal, or refer to guides like our live blog that use price trackers for you. And if you have an Amazon Prime membership, make the most of it.

While I’m personally a trackpad guy through and through, I know plenty of people who prefer a mouse, and the power users among them all agree on which one.

If you’re planning to use the new MacBook Pro as part of a desk setup, I’d pair it with Anker’s 10-in-1 Smart Display hub. A height-adjustable laptop stand like this one from Native Union can round out the setup nicely if you already have, or plan to add, an external keyboard and mouse.

If you’re anything like, you’ll want to have a neat and tidy place to stow your MacBook when at home, at your desk. While I prefer to have it right on the table top surface when in use, if I’m docking up to a multi-display setup with a mouse and keyboard, or working another system at my desk, I like to have a nice stand option to have it up on display and visible. Twelve South makes some great models, and there are some ultra-affordable variants I have used in the past from Nulaxy that have stood the test of time and work great.

A fast external SSD is one of my favorite accessories for a new MacBook Pro. I use the original OWC Express 1M2 and really like its aluminum heat sink design and silent operation. The newer Express 1M2 80G keeps that same appeal while taking advantage of Thunderbolt 5, with OWC advertising speeds over 6,000MB/s. It’s the version I’d pick for a new MacBook Pro, especially for working with large video projects, offloading photo libraries, or backing up files without filling up the Mac’s internal storage.

#3355. Ring's New $250 Indoor Camera Drone Sounds Terrifying

Ring made its name with its smart doorbells with built-in cameras, and now sells more indoor cameras than any other company, capturing more than 40% of the market. When you've already moved tens of millions of devices (enough to raise serious concerns about their use as part of the surveillance state), you always need to keep innovating, and today, the company announced a product it has been working on for a decade: an indoor camera drone powered by artificial intelligence. I got a chance to check it out during a media event yesterday, and I can report that, as harbingers of our dystopian future go, it is only mildly terrifying.

The drone camera is one of two products in the company's new Ring Robotics line, alongside a "rover cam" that looks kind of like the canister of a vacuum cleaner attached to an iPad. While the Ring Rover Cam is priced at $999.99 and targeted at businesses, the Ring Drone Cam is a much more affordable $249.99, reasonable enough that it will appeal to consumers looking for another way to keep (robot) eyes on their stuff.

The drone camera records 2K video and has a 148-degree field of view and the ability to rotate 360 degrees. It works with existing Ring cameras, doorbells, sensors, and alarms, as well as the Alexa Home Map. It has a flight time of eight minutes, and once it returns to its base station, it takes around an hour to fully recharge (eight minutes on the dock will give it one minute in the air).

As Ring founder Jamie Siminoff explained during the preview event, the company has been trying to build a workable camera drone for around a decade, but couldn't overcome certain design challenges until the advancement of AI models that allow the device to handle most of the computing—from route programming to threat detection—via the cloud, so the drones can be smaller and lighter.

According to Ring, when setting up the Ring Drone Cam, you carry it around your house, allowing it to map the interior. It will "intelligently identify rooms and suggest patrol points: spots worth extra attention." When sent out on "patrol," the drone's AI pilot will travel between hotspots, sensing and avoiding furniture and other obstacles along the way.The Ring Drone Cam works with other Ring cameras, so if an alert is triggered somewhere in your home—say, a window opening unexpectedly—the drone will take off to investigate. It has a built-in security light that will make its presence known, so it can also act as a deterrent, though the screaming sound of its spinning propellers will accomplish that just as well.

According to Ring, the drone camera can deliver peace of mind whether you're home or away, and admittedly I do like the idea of being able to check on my pets or make sure no pipes have burst while I'm at work or on vacation (though admittedly you can get the same sort of monitoring without involving an AI device that looks like a mini version of the flying robots from The Terminator).

I admit that the Ring Drone Cam seems pretty cool, provided I don't think about it too much. I don't know that I really feel the need to have every inch of my home covered in security cameras, but I do like the idea that the drone could, for example, go to check out what's going on if one of my smoke alarms' temperature sensors reports that one spot in the house is all of a sudden hotter than it should be.

If you're ready to enter this brave new world of security, you'll have to wait a bit longer: The Ring Drone Camera isn't expected to ship until January 2027, but you can sign up to be alerted when it is available for preorder now.

#3352. He Thinks Malaysia Airlines Flight 370 Was Teleported. Thousands of People Believe Him

O n March 8, 2014, Malaysia Airlines Flight 370 was en route from Kuala Lumpur to Beijing when it disappeared from radar over the Indian Ocean, sparking the most expensive search in aviation history, wall-to-wall global news coverage, and even rare public protests within China. The mystery captured the hearts and minds of millions of people across the world, but there was no closure or catharsis for the families of those missing. In an age of seemingly ubiquitous satellite coverage, the plane’s final resting place — and that of the 239 people onboard — remains an open question.

But a man named Ashton Forbes believes he has the answer: The U.S. military teleported the passenger jet in a show of might against China. Armed with a pair of dramatic videos that appear to show the aircraft vanishing, Forbes has spent the past three years posting relentlessly on X and YouTube, trying to convince everyone that the military used orb-like vessels to instantaneously teleport MH370 out of the sky. On its face, his theory appears impossible. So why do so many people believe him?

Since he started posting about the unlikely theory in 2023, Forbes — a 44-year-old healthcare IT consultant from St. Paul, Minnesota, with a close-cropped side-parting, rectangular glasses, and well-ironed plaid shirts — has become a divisive cult figure in the online UFO-obsessed hinterland. In the uniquely sparse information vacuum surrounding the fate of the plane, Forbes has positioned himself as the radical, crusading thought leader with the far-reaching answer that doubles up as the confirmation that truly magical feats are possible.

In an age of increasingly sophisticated deepfakes and deepening distrust, Forbes’ rise from anonymous Reddit lurker to conspiracy-world talking head reflects a broader phenomenon. With 78 percent of Americans believing the government knows more about UFOs than it is telling the public, and 37 percent convinced that some unidentified flying objects are alien spacecraft, his claims tap into a widespread suspicion that there is more out there — and that this is only the latest example of the government refusing to admit what the U.S. military knows, and can do.  Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century

Forbes, who has a fear of flying — “Every time I get on a plane, I assume it’s the last thing I’ll do” — was a self-described “lurker in the UFO community” when he clocked the videos on Reddit in August 2023. The footage ignited a frenzy of speculation after someone on the r/UFOs subreddit claimed in a viral thread that the videos showed “UFOs stealing an airliner out of the sky and teleporting away with it.”

Despite his sympathy toward the possibility of extraterrestrial life, Forbes dismissed the idea that an alien civilization would meddle with humanity so simplistically. “Aliens are so advanced, we’re like ants to them,” he tells Rolling Stone. “It’s more likely we’re a zoo.”

It made more sense to him that the U.S. military was behind it. According to Forbes, the military secretly developed fusion-powered technology capable of manipulating the space-time continuum. “The government has figured out how to turn an electromagnetic beam into a gravitational one,” Forbes says. “This is the United States versus China.” The teleportation of MH370, he says, was a message for America’s enemies, and that China’s intelligence services know what happened. “We can end them anytime we want,” he says. Of course, there is no evidence that any of this technology exists — if the plane was in fact “ported,” it would upend our understanding of physics, warfare, and the nature of reality itself.

On his X feed, Forbes has railed at “libtards,” claimed his detractors are “clinically insane narcissists,” accused the government of “LARPing about revealing UFOs,” and mourned the death of Patrick Stewart. He will appear in Tucker Carlson’s forthcoming documentary series, Shadow Figures, which advances another theory about MH370: that an explosion brought it down.

At first, his liberal family feared Forbes, who is single, might have had “a psychological break or something … As time went on, they had to find a way to cope with it,” he says, noting that they simply refuse to engage in discussions about MH370 with him. He also told his employer of the past 20 years that “I’m doing something completely crazy, and I think I’m exposing my own government.” The company, which he does not wish to name, reviewed his social media, Forbes says, “and they said it was basically fine as long as I just put my own opinions and avoid talking about them.”

THOUGH FEVERED SPECULATION SURROUNDS the fate of MH370, we do have substantial evidence about the aircraft’s final movements. According to analysis of the plane’s automated satellite communications, after losing contact with air-traffic control, it continued flying for hours. Investigators concluded that it had most likely flown south into the Indian Ocean, off the coast of western Australia, where it was presumed to have crashed.

Around 30 pieces of suspected debris from the plane have washed ashore along the east African coast and islands in the western Indian Ocean, three of which were confirmed to be from MH370. But the main wreckage remains undiscovered, and investigators have never definitively established why the aircraft changed course, or who turned off its transponder.

Suspicions of a cover-up emerged almost immediately. In the wake of the plane’s disappearance, the former prime minister of Malaysia, Mahathir Mohamad, accused the CIA of “hiding” its whereabouts. “Airplanes don’t just disappear,” he wrote. “Certainly not these days.” On his blog, Mohamed cited a 2006 article which apparently claimed that the CIA has the power to operate aircraft “remotely by radio or satellite … if terrorists attempt to gain control of the flight deck.” (The CIA did not respond to a request for comment.)

Forbes, who describes himself as a skeptic and says the only other conspiracy he entertains is that a government operative may have assassinated John F. Kennedy, would come to share Mohamad’s suspicion of U.S. government involvement. The immediate response to the plane going missing was the first sign that something was going on. “They have this plane going dark 40 minutes after it takes off, [then] it flies over Malaysia,” but the Malaysian government doesn’t send any jets to track it. (The Malaysian government’s initial response was criticized as lackluster, though it ultimately led an unprecedented search mission, dispatching 334 search flights over 1.7 million square miles.) “This plane goes into the Andaman Sea, they lose track of it and let it drift off into somewhere where we don’t know where it went.”

Forbes’ search for the whereabouts of the plane began nine years later. The teleportation videos were apparently first posted on YouTube in the weeks after the plane went missing by RegicideAnon, “a UFO uploader account,” which, by Forbes’ own admission, mostly posted discreditable clips before the channel itself disappeared. But it had no impact for almost a decade, until RegicideAnon suddenly took the r/UFO subreddit by storm in the summer of 2023. The videos had resurfaced after Department of Defense whistleblower David Grusch testified in front of Congress about his knowledge of unidentified aerial phenomena, or UAP. Though he didn’t make the connection, Redditors did.

In the low-resolution footage, which Forbes believes was taken by U.S. military drones, what appears to be a passenger jet is flying through a cloudy, hazy blue sky when three small, saucer-shaped white objects — or “plasma orbs,” as Forbes calls them, supposedly containing fusion reactors — suddenly appear and circle the plane with increasing speed. Then there is a flash, and the plane disappears. “I was like, ‘Dude, what is this?’” he says.

Forbes got to work quickly, inventorying “what it would take to ‘hoax’ the videos.” In a 28-point list posted on X, he speculated that it would have taken anywhere from four to 72 days to make the videos, that the hoaxer would need to re-create what MH370 looked like, know what the turn radius of a Boeing 777 is at a certain altitude, and know “how to animate orbs.” Forbes is no expert, with his business degree from Washington University in St. Louis, but he concluded that it was more likely the videos were real than that someone would have gone to such lengths to fabricate them. He pledged to give $150,000 to anyone who conclusively proved that the videos have been faked.

Some, however, say it wouldn’t have been too difficult. According to visual effects expert Niko Pueringer, whose YouTube channel Corridor Crew has debunked the videos, a VFX artist back in 2014 could have created them in a couple of days. “There are plenty of giveaways in the MH370 animation, but it is executed so well, and with such a perfect eye to style and dramatic timing, that it gets us to emotionally respond,” he says. “If you can create a fantastical image, but give it the texture of real footage, you are pulling off a magic trick. If you can elevate it by placing it within a story, you end up hitting something really primal in every human being.”

Other VFX experts have highlighted “glaring” compositing errors that allegedly reveal the videos were fabricated from various multimedia sources. When the plane disappears with a sudden flash, the two videos appear to be slightly out of sync (which Forbes vehemently disputes), while the clouds are said to be unchanging and the moving objects exhibit no motion blur. Pueringer has also pointed to an apparent match between the flash in the videos and a stock explosion effect from the 1990s, which had been used in video games.

Yet a stronger blow came to Forbes when his critics traced the clouds in one of the videos to aerial photographs taken years earlier. One sleuth even claimed to have discovered the source file behind them and purported to have linked the cloud photographs to a NASA weather satellite, before their account was recently taken down. Forbes has an explanation: These photographs “must have been planted online by the U.S. intelligence agencies” in a type of false-flag operation to confuse the public further and are “objectively fake.” Forbes has so far not dispensed his promised $150,000. “When you start to realize I’m right, you’ll start to see these patterns,” he says. “[The government is] influencing our thoughts all the time.”

In the face of criticism, the scope of Forbes’ claims expanded far beyond the videos themselves. Toward the end of 2023, he supposedly figured out who had leaked them: a former lieutenant commander in the Navy who pleaded guilty in 2017 to mishandling classified information. (He could not be reached for comment.)

There is no publicly available evidence connecting the former serviceperson to the MH370 videos, but Forbes says classified portions of his case must conceal the answer. “It has to be him because everything lines up: right time, right place, right access, and right punishment,” he says. “How can it not be those videos? Tell me anything else it could be that he leaked.”

One day in February 2024, Forbes thought he’d hit the jackpot. Joe Rogan messaged him on X with an invitation to his show. “Hey, man, I’m watching this YouTube video of you talking about Malaysia Airlines,” Rogan wrote. “Fascinating stuff. I’d love to talk to you about this.” The influential podcaster had recently interviewed a former U.S. intelligence official who claimed the government was secretly attempting to reverse-engineer alien spacecraft.

“Anytime you want, Joe. I just want to say I’m a normal guy, and this rabbit hole has been really wild,” Forbes wrote back, according to a screenshot of the chat shared with Rolling Stone. “A lot of the stuff you’ve been saying about UFOs being drones, our technology, etc., lines up with exactly what I’ve come to realize through this investigation.”

Rogan said that his team could book his travel and hotel, but then he put on the brakes. “Hey, man, I’m gonna put a pause on this episode until I can clarify whether or not this is a hoax,” Rogan wrote. “I’ve been going down the rabbit hole, and there’s a lot of evidence that those videos are special effects.” Forbes sent him reams of messages claiming they are real. In a later episode, Rogan dismissed the videos as “bullshit.” Forbes messaged Rogan with a link to the clip, saying, “Bro, what is this? Lmao.”

Despite the setback, Forbes was undeterred, appearing on conservative commentator Candace Owens’ podcast in October 2024 for a friendly interview that amassed 1.7 million views. By then, Forbes had metamorphosed the MH370 enigma into the foundation for a considerably larger theory of reality, centered on the existence of a hidden, virtually limitless source of energy that could revolutionize civilization. “There was a day where, I realized, this is all about free energy,” Forbes told Owens, “if you connect and follow the dots, and the science, if you ask yourself, ‘Where is the energy from these self-sustaining, coherent orbs coming from?’”

He was no longer merely arguing that the U.S. military possessed technology capable of making an airliner disappear, or — as he later began to — that most UFO sightings actually pertain to U.S.-government orbs. “It’s all just fusion,” he says. Forbes became ardent in his belief that humanity already possessed the means to extract virtually limitless energy from the fabric of the universe — and he invested $5,000 into a purported “free-energy” device, which he started promoting.

Forbes acknowledged his mistake, saying he had been sent a photograph of what he believed was a similar design and misunderstood what he was looking at. His belief in the technology itself, however, remained intact. “What I showed was a real free-energy device,” he told the UAP Unidentified Alien Podcast in August 2024. “Absolutely real.” Forbes insists that he has “never directly sold anything to profit off the [MH370] case, but tried to promote a lot of podcasts and other small businesses.”

Three years into his quest, Forbes is still gaining traction, with one recent X post notching 17,000 likes and 1.5 million views. “239 people died on this plane, in an operation the U.S. will never admit to, using technology that shouldn’t exist,” he wrote. “No one is fighting for them except my community [the 14,000-acolyte MH370x on X]. We’re proud of it, because despite how insane it seems, we know it’s true. They teleported that plane.”

The evidence bolstering the hypothesis, in his view, only continues to accumulate. In the White House’s Sept. 18 release of “UAP Encounter” files, one of the documents shows that the Defense Intelligence Agency commissioned a report on “traversable wormholes and ‘stargates’ … that theoretically offer a means of faster-than-light travel.” Forbes tweeted: “I’m literally being proven correct in real time, and it’s amazing.” In another tweet, he added: “Proves our reality is a hologram.” (The wormhole report is a theoretical document.)

The fact that the Trump administration has also been trumpeting America’s technological prowess in language borrowed from science fiction has only helped Forbes. Last year, White House science adviser Michael Kratsios claimed in a missive celebrating American technological supremacy that U.S. innovations “permit us to manipulate time and space” and “leave distance annihilated.” He was speaking broadly about scientific and technological progress, rather than announcing a physics-defying weapon, but he concluded his speech reiterating that new “scientific discoveries … will bend time and space, make more with less, and drive us further into the endless frontier.”

Forbes isn’t necessarily opposed to the U.S. being in charge of the endless frontier. On Sept. 23, he was on Alex Jones Live, effectively celebrating that the U.S. has an “asymmetrical advantage” over its enemies — and one which it should be leveraging because it won’t last forever. “That was a message in 2014 to China, Iran, Russia, North Korea — that we have something that you don’t have, and we control this planet,” Forbes said. “They’re using these fusion reactors to manipulate space-time.” For his part, Jones agreed that it was “the biggest conspiracy in human history, that free energy and teleportation are real.” Trending Stories Sade Are Not Attending Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Induction Ceremony The ‘You Can See Everything’ Interview You’ve Been Waiting For Watch Ariana Grande, Ben Stiller, Robert De Niro Take Over ‘The Tonight Show’ Trump Finally Gets Around to Claiming the Midterms Were Rigged

For all the extraordinary claims Forbes has made about secret military technology and the nature of reality, his convictions ultimately rest on two pieces of evidence. He admits that his entire worldview “is solely because I watched them teleport that Malaysian airliner. That’s why they hide this secret so fiercely. If they told the truth, everything would crumble.”

He says there are ways to prove him wrong: Find the person who made the videos, find the plane, talk to the lieutenant commander, or get the U.S. government to make a statement about the footage. “Those are the only ways to prove the videos fake,” he says, “and the debunkers hate it because they know they can’t do any of those things.”

#3351. Report: Apple saved over $5 billion in taxes through Singapore and Ireland in 2026

A new Financial Times report reveals how Apple saved billions in taxes in 2026 by shifting profits through Singapore and Ireland. Here are the details.

A few days ago, Apple published its annual Form 10-K, as required by the SEC, containing detailed information about its financial performance and operations for its 2026 fiscal year.

Included in the form, as the FT noted, is information regarding how Apple reduced its tax bill by billions of dollars through its operations in Singapore and Ireland.

For years, Apple’s tax arrangements in Ireland were the subject of scrutiny, culminating in a 2024 ruling by the EU’s top court that required the company to pay €13 billion in back taxes. Apple completed the payment in 2025.

That came a few years after Apple announced plans to bring most of its $252 billion in overseas cash back to the US, following tax reforms introduced during Donald Trump’s first administration.

Since then, to discourage companies from shifting profits to countries with lower tax rates, more than 130 countries have agreed to introduce a minimum corporate tax rate of 15% for large multinational companies, as part of a 2021 initiative coordinated by the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD).

Under the agreement, companies that pay less than 15% in a particular country may face additional taxes to make up the difference. The new rules also resulted in an additional $2.5 billion in taxes for Apple in Singapore in 2026, according to the company’s SEC filing.

Ireland adopted the new rules in 2024, followed by Singapore in 2025.

Back to the FT’s report, it notes that new US accounting rules now require publicly traded companies to disclose when their taxes on overseas profits differ significantly from the 21% US federal corporate tax rate.

These new requirements revealed that Apple saved $2.7 billion in taxes through Singapore in 2026, surpassing the $2.6 billion it saved through Ireland.

If Apple had been taxed on all of its global profits in 2026 at the US federal rate, it would have incurred a total bill of $33bn — demonstrating the scale of the $5bn tax reduction it received from booking profits in Ireland and Singapore. The company incurred corporation taxes totalling $27bn this year.

The FT also noted that Apple’s effective tax rate in Singapore fluctuated around 10% between 2023 and 2025, but is expected to approach 15% under the new rules. Singapore’s standard corporate tax rate is 17%.
